PythonExport.Name: ShapeListPy

Documentation.UserDocu:
A list of sub elements of a shape, which behaves like a list of Part.Shape.
What Shape.Faces and its siblings answer with. It is a VIEW of the shape it came from: it materialises an element only when one is asked for, so its length and any single element of it cost one cache lookup rather than a shape object per element:
len(shape.Faces) # does not build a single face shape.Faces[0] # builds one face for f in shape.Faces: # builds them as the loop reaches them
The elements are the ones the shape had when the list was asked for; a later change to that shape does not reach back into the list.
Everything a read-only list does, this does: indexing, slicing (which answers with a plain list), iteration, len(), "in", "+" with any sequence, "*", ==, index() and count(). Writing to it -- append(), sort(), pop() and the rest -- makes it a value of its own first, copying every element out of the shape; that list shares its storage with any copy of itself until one of them is written to.

copy() -> ShapeList: a copy of this list.
It shares this list's storage until one of them is written to, so it costs a pointer however long the list is.

index(Shape) -> int: the position of a shape in this list.
Raises ValueError when the shape is not in it. A view answers from the shape's own cache rather than by walking the list.
count(Shape) -> int: how many entries are that shape.

append(Shape) -> None: add one shape at the end.
Makes the list a value of its own first.
extend(iterable) -> None: add every shape of an iterable.
insert(index, Shape) -> None: insert one shape before index.
pop([index]) -> Shape: remove and return one entry, the last by default.
remove(Shape) -> None: remove the first entry that is that shape.
reverse() -> None: reverse the list in place.

sort(key=None, reverse=False) -> None: sort the list in place.
Takes what list.sort() takes and means the same by it.
How many elements the list has. Same as len().
The shape type of the elements, e.g. 'Face'. 'Shape' for a list of mixed sub shapes.
Whether the list is still a view of the shape it came from, i.e. whether nothing has been written to it.
The shape a view came from, or None once the list is a value of its own.
